newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangling suspended on Ford deal.
newsitem.headline: Jiangling suspended on Ford deal.

text.p: The Shenzhen stock exchange on Wednesday suspended trading in shares of Jiangling Motors Corp after the company said it plans to issue new B shares, the Shenzhen-based Securities News said.

The newspaper said the company's board of directors proposed to issue 170 million additional B shares and allocate 120 million shares to Ford Motor Co, the statement said. The plan will need the approval of shareholders.
Ford Motor Co said in a statement on Wednesday that it would increase its investment in Jiangling Motors with the purchase of 120 million B shares worth $54.5 million.

Ford and Jiangling have entered into a subscription agreement under which Ford has agreed to increase its equity share in its Chinese partner to approximately 30 percent from the current 20 percent, the statement said.
Jiangling's statement said it would discuss with Ford the price of Ford's B share batch.

The statement said the company would finalise the B share plan at a shareholders' meeting scheduled for April 30 and would apply to the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's securities watchdog, for approval.
If the new deal gets the go-ahead, Ford will hold 258.64 million Jiangling B shares, accounting for 29.96 percent of the firm's total outstanding shares, the statement said.
Ford would also remain the company's second largest shareholder, it said.
Ford currently holds 138.64 million B shares, accounting for 20 percent of Jiangling's outstanding shares.
Ford's new purchase would help boost cooperation between the two motor firms, Jiangling said.
